cues.text: It ties the payroll register, the list of every paycheck, to all 2,493 paychecks. One flag: two employees are paid into the same bank account.
It rebuilds eight sample paychecks. A workers' insurance deduction is slightly too high on overtime.
The payroll manager entered her own raise with no signed approval. The shared account belongs to a married couple.
It ties payroll to the books and all four quarterly tax returns. But $22,864 of employer payroll tax for June was never booked in June.
Last, it adds up what it found against materiality and writes the workpapers for the CPA.

All done. Known mistakes add up to just over $25,000, well under materiality, including about $2,500 owed back to the crews. The bigger issue is control: the unapproved raise. Seven items stay open. The CPA, a person, concludes and signs. The machine gives no opinion.
